newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First to announce options later today.
newsitem.headline: NZ First to announce options later today.

text.p: New Zealand First leader Winston Peters on Tuesday convened the first caucus meeting since the general election still refusing to indicate which party he would join in government.
Peters said he would announce the options open to the New Zealand First after the caucus meeting.
New MP Peter Brown told Reuters before the meeting he expected caucus to settle the team that would negotiate with other parties.
"I think all we will decide is the negotiating team," Brown said.
Other MPs Jack Elder, Ron Mark and John Delamere said they had an open mind about whether the party supported National or Labour.
Asked if his previous membership of the National Party was influencing his decision, Te Tai Rawhiti MP Delamere told Reuters: "No not at all."
He said National had been sued on his behalf over breaches of candidate selection rules in the past.

Asked if he accepted Maori would prefer New Zealand First to go with Labour he said: "Quite a few have suggested that, but one should not lose sight of the fact they abandoned Labour... not as much (on the list vote) -- that will happen next time.
"Certainly there is an empathy. It is like you've left your parents and you still have that relationship. We will weigh up what is best and go back and consult.
"But they elected us to do the job and we will do the best possible for New Zealand First, and for Maori and pakeha. All options are open as far as I am concerned," Delamere said.
New Zealand First president Doug Woolerton said the party would take the negotiation process slowly and carefully. "We will take as long as necessary," Woolerton said.
He declined to comment on whether support for a Labour-led or National-led minority government was an option.
